newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland business confidence dips on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland business confidence dips on uncertainty.

text.p: Business confidence in Northern Ireland has dropped 25 per cent amid resurgent violence and political instability, according to a survey by the Confederation of British Industry (CBI).
"It is likely that business confidence will not return while the current atmosphere of political instability persists," said Deirdre Stewart, assistant director of the CBI in Northern Ireland.

The survey was taken in the last two weeks of December and the first two days of the New Year - when Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrillas renewed a campaign against British rule with attacks on targets in Belfast.
It showed a 25 percent drop in confidence in the local economy compared with the last survey two months ago.

The British government says Northern Ireland is one of the best-performing regions of the United Kingdom in terms of job creation and growth but has expressed serious concern about the outlook after the IRA ended a ceasefire in February last year.

The IRA said in a New Year's message that they wanted to take part in a peace process but would continue their guerrilla war until their political wing, Sinn Fein, was invited to the talks without preconditions.
The survey said business circles in Northern Ireland were increasingly concerned about the political outlook for the province.

Belfast peace talks resume next week. Sinn Fein is excluded until the IRA declares a permanent end to violence but all other parties at the talks say they will press ahead with the negotiations to try to find a lasting settlement.
